chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn 'Imran al-Halabi, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The mu'adhdhin (caller to prayer) is forgiven for the extent of his voice, and everything that hears him bears witness for him.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'And the adhan is not valid for any of the prayers before its time enters, up to his saying: 'And there is no harm for a person to give the adhan while he is not in a state of wudu.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for the caller to prayer (mu'adhdhin) and is wudu required for the adhan?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the mu'adhdhin's role as a witness to the call to prayer, with his forgiveness spanning the distance his voice carries and all listeners testifying for him. Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies the legal nuance that while the adhan must precede the prayer time to be valid, the caller is not required to be in a state of ritual purity (wudu) when reciting it, reflecting the practical flexibility in Shia fiqh for this specific act of worship.
